summary: 1934 CCC-built 100-foot tower in Badoura State Forest near Akeley; staffed until 1979, still used by nursery staff; sources disagree on the maker.

facts.design: 100-foot stairway tower with a metal cab; the Register says Aermotor, the Hubbard County list says McClintock Marshall

access.note: Still used by Badoura Forest Nursery personnel as a radio antenna and emergency lookout; no public climbing is described. Easily seen from Highway 64.

events.note: Site has been a state tree nursery since 1933, per the Hubbard County list
Built by the CCC and the Minnesota Division of Forestry to oversee an area of high fire danger; tower 61 on the county list
Staffed until 1979, when air detection replaced it

notes_for_editor: Maker is disputed and not resolved: the Register says Aermotor; the Hubbard County list says McClintock Marshall stairway tower. The 'restricted' access level is inferred from the Register's note that nursery personnel use the tower; no closure notice or access rule was found, and the state forest page we fetched had no readable text. Current condition rests on the Register alone. The 1933 nursery date is from the county list only and was not checked against a DNR page. The Forest Lookouts page is a hobbyist site reproducing data; it is used only for the 1934 height. No photos added.
